_comment: MUTATION TESTING ASKS WHETHER THE TESTS WOULD NOTICE. A suite that passes against broken code will pass against a real regression too, and this repository has had two of those: a baseline gate that was computed and ignored, and a count from a model that killed the run. Both passed every test that existed.
_comment_mutate: Where a wrong answer is silent. The domain decides what counts as a proof, what identifies a finding and what stops a build, so a mutation there produces a report that reads exactly like a correct one. Measured cost with the command runner: about twenty seconds a mutant, which is why this runs nightly rather than on a push.
_comment_ignore: The sandbox is a copy of the project, and a copied transform cache is the unmutated source: vitest served it and every mutant survived. dist is not needed either, since the test that drives the built binary is the one test left out of this run.
_comment_thresholds: MEASURED, NOT ASPIRED TO: a partial pass over the policies killed 119 of 176 mutants with 6 timeouts, about 71 per cent, which is the same neighbourhood as the Symfony twin's 72. The gate sits under it so it catches a real regression rather than failing every night, and the number is written here so raising or lowering it later is a visible decision.
